processes.title: Run the code quality check
processes.summary: Publish this repository's code quality: the score box at the bottom of README.md with its breakdown, the refactoring plan, and the site definition refreshed on the way. Changes no source code. Ends as a pull request on a quality/check-<date> branch.

processes.title: Run the widget identification
sentences: where are the widgets written by hand
processes.summary: Identify the widgets: every route as a user sees it, in the widget notation, with every place a view writes by hand the markup a catalogue widget should own. Read-only - no branch, no commit, no pull request, no score box. It identifies the widgets; it never adopts them.

processes.title: Run the input validation check
sentences: check the inputs against the schema
can anything write data that does not fit its column
is the MCP server validating its inputs
processes.summary: Check every entry point that writes - API routes, server actions, command handlers, MCP tool and action handlers - against the column types and constraints it writes to: guarded, mismatched, unguarded, form only or repaired. Read-only - no branch, no commit, no pull request, no score box. It finds the gaps; fixing them is a fix/ branch the person asks for.

processes.title: Refactor the repo
processes.summary: One measured round on a refactor/round-N branch, taking the next steps from the top of the refactoring plan in order. Behaviour never changes. This is the one process that changes source code.

processes.title: Set up the widget designs
sentences: Check the site against the brand
Check the widgets against their designs
processes.summary: The brand sheet and each widget's design sheet, and checking the site against them. Optional: only a repository with a widget catalogue has designs to keep. A question gets the reading and changes nothing; a Check fixes the widget on a branch.

processes.title: Run end of day
processes.summary: The refactor round if one is due, the check that the connector covers what changed today, the plain-English work log on the day's tasks, and the day's branch pushed with its pull request open.

processes.title: What is the code quality score?
sentences: What is the code quality score?
processes.summary: The score and whether the gate passes, read only. No branch, no commit, nothing published - this is the reading, not the code quality check.

processes.title: Is a refactor round due?
sentences: how many deploys since the baseline
processes.summary: The commits on the default branch since the baseline was last committed, against the rhythm. Read-only.
